name: solved

phase_0.boundary_condition: The solved theorem that the alternating prime series has no monotone tail, formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib

VINIT.chosen_element: series definition ∑(-1)^n n/p_n with a_n = n/p_n
VINIT.justification: Void initial state before the sequence and its properties are named

TANCH.chosen_element: terminal theorem: no monotone tail exists for (a_n)
TANCH.justification: Closed boundary containing the entire proof and its formalization

AFWD.chosen_element: forward derivation steps: ratio comparison → cross-multiplication → gap substitution → rise criterion
AFWD.justification: Directed transformation from series definition to exact algebraic rise condition n·g_n < p_n

AREV.chosen_element: reverse application of bounded gaps theorem and prime number theorem to specific indices
AREV.justification: Descent from general analytic theorems (Zhang-Maynard-Polymath, PNT) to concrete witness n ≥ max(N,M)

CLINK.chosen_element: composition of rise criterion with gap bounds and superlinearity
CLINK.justification: Sequential chaining: n·g_n ≤ n·B < p_n composes bounded gaps and superlinearity into a rise

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: self-reference of the rise criterion and the formalized proof object
IMSCRIB.justification: The criterion n·g_n < p_n ⇔ a_n < a_{n+1} is an identity; the Lean proof knows its own structure

FSPLIT.chosen_element: fork on the proposition ∃N ∀n≥N: a_{n+1} ≤ a_n (monotone tail exists)
FSPLIT.justification: Splits into T-arm (assume monotone tail, derive contradiction) and F-arm (prove no monotone tail directly)

FFUSE.chosen_element: rejoin of contradiction arm (B) and direct proof arm (T) into paradice state
FFUSE.justification: Arms rejoin via Belnap join: T-arm holds both monotone assumption and derived rise (B), F-arm holds no-monotone-tail (T), fuse yields B

EVALT.chosen_element: affirmation of the monotone tail assumption on the T-arm
EVALT.justification: Constructive truth of the assumed hypothesis before it generates its own negation

EVALF.chosen_element: negation of monotone tail on the F-arm; failure of alternating series test monotone hypothesis
EVALF.justification: Constructive falsity of the monotone tail proposition, established by bounded gaps + superlinearity

ENGAGR.chosen_element: paradice on T-arm: monotone assumption and derived rise simultaneously held
ENGAGR.justification: The contradiction does not explode — the assumption and its negation at witness n are both live (B state)

IFIX.chosen_element: permanent record: theorem formalized in Lean 4 depending on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
IFIX.justification: Irreversible fixation of the proof in a proof assistant; append-only mathematical record

split_outputs: T-arm: assume true, derive contradiction via witness n
F-arm: prove false via bounded gaps + superlinearity
phase_2.fuse_element: rejoin of contradiction and direct proof
phase_2.fuse_result: B state (paradice) — both the contradictory assumption and the constructive non-monotonicity proof are held
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: Before the series ∑(-1)^n n/p_n is defined; no sequence, no gaps, no criterion
phase_3.true_description: A rise is constructively witnessed at a specific index n (n·g_n < p_n verified)
phase_3.false_description: The monotone tail proposition is constructively refuted; alternating series test hypothesis fails
phase_3.both_description: The T-arm holds the monotone assumption and its negation at the same witness n; the fused theorem state is a paradice

steps.domain_action: Initialize the alternating prime series ∑(-1)^n n/p_n with magnitudes a_n = n/p_n
The sequence definition self-references as the object of study
Forward transform — compare consecutive ratios n/p_n < (n+1)/p_{n+1}
Compose — cross-multiply to n·p_{n+1} < (n+1)·p_n
Forward transform — substitute p_{n+1} = p_n + g_n yielding n·g_n < p_n
Compose — cancel n·p_n to obtain the exact rise criterion a_n < a_{n+1} ⇔ n·g_n < p_n
The rise criterion self-knows as an algebraic identity
Fork on the proposition ∃N ∀n≥N: a_{n+1} ≤ a_n (monotone tail exists)
T-arm — affirm the monotone tail assumption as constructive truth
T-arm — forward: fix such N for contradiction
T-arm — forward: invoke bounded gaps theorem (B=246 infinitely often)
T-arm — forward: invoke superlinearity p_n/n → ∞ giving M with n·246 < p_n for n≥M
T-arm — compose: choose n ≥ max(N,M) with g_n ≤ 246
T-arm — forward: at this n, n·g_n ≤ n·246 < p_n so a_n < a_{n+1} (rise)
T-arm — paradice: monotone assumption and derived rise simultaneously held (B state)
F-arm — reverse: bounded gaps theorem (Zhang-Maynard-Polymath) descends to g_n ≤ 246 infinitely often
F-arm — reverse: prime number theorem descends to p_n/n → ∞ (superlinearity)
F-arm — compose: for any N, ∃n≥N with g_n ≤ 246 and n·246 < p_n
F-arm — forward: rise criterion gives a_n < a_{n+1} at this n
F-arm — negative: no monotone tail exists (constructive falsity of the proposition)
Fuse T-arm (B) and F-arm (T) — Belnap join yields B (paradice held)
Reverse to alternating series test context — the test requires eventual monotone decrease
The monotone decrease hypothesis of the alternating series test fails on every tail
Forward: convergence of ∑(-1)^n n/p_n, if it holds, must come from cancellation of paired terms
Compose: the gap sequence g_n determines the cancellation structure
Permanent fixation — theorem formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib
Permanent fixation — proof depends on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
The formalized proof self-references its own syntactic structure
Terminal anchor — the solved theorem closes the system

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Lean 4 kernel translating mathematical intentions into type-theoretic operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Mathlib library providing prime number theory, analysis, and order structures as shared components
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Proof state stored as Lean terms with metavariables; tactics manipulate the proof context
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Tactic script order determines operation sequence; `have` statements create intermediate goals
phase_5.alfs_store: The Lean 4 formalization repository (Mathlib) as canonical bootstrap store for number theory

phase_6.cycle_cost: One tactic application per proof step; each `have` or `apply` consumes a goal and produces subgoals
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Open goal state with hypotheses in context; metavariables mark unfinished proof obligations
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Closed goal state (no metavariables); proof term constructed and type-checked
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — each tactic step preserves logical equivalence; the proof term is a reversible witness up to definitional equality

banked_count_check.verdict: 4 unit(s) of weight cleared with nothing banked behind them: the count was in the open when the reversal came
banked_count_check.remedy: open the region that holds the result BEFORE the region that computes it, and close them in that order, so the inner fuse folds into the enclosing frame rather than into the register
